other_opex.text: Borrowed funds from various sources are generally used to supplement deposit growth and meet other operating needs. Customers’ borrowings include short-term and long-term advances from the FHLB, FRB, federal funds purchased, senior unsecured notes and subordinated debt. Subordinated debt is also considered as Tier 2 capital for certain regulatory calculations.

prov.heading: Provision for credit losses
prov.text: The $1.1 million decrease in the provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 included a $0.9 million increase in provision for credit losses on loans and leases for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, which primarily reflects a reserve build in multifamily loans driven by market specific conditions as well as increased reserves for consumer installment loans. These were largely offset by reserve releases in commercial and industrial and commercial real estate non-owner occupied loans attributable to slightly improving macroeconomic variables. The ACL on loans and leases held for investment represented 1.02% of total loans and leases receivable at September 30, 2026, compared to 1.03% of total loans and leases receivable at September 30, 2025. Net charge-offs for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $12.7 million, or 28 basis points of average loans and leases on an annualized basis, compared to net charge-offs of $15.4 million, or 39 basis points on an annualized basis, for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

nonint.heading: Non-interest expense
nonint.text:
The $8.2 million increase in non-interest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily resulted from increases of $7.5 million in salaries and employee benefits, $4.7 million in technology, communication and bank operations, $3.7 million in commercial lease depreciation and $1.7 million in other non-interest expense. These increases were offset in part by decreases of $4.5 million in professional fees and $3.8 million in FDIC assessments, non-income taxes and regulatory fees for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

The $25.7 million increase in non-interest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025 primarily resulted from increases of $26.4 million in salaries and employee benefits, $12.0 million in commercial lease depreciation, $7.5 million in technology, communication and bank operations and $4.7 million in other non-interest expense. These increases were offset in part by decreases of $14.6 million in FDIC assessments, non-income taxes and regulatory fees and $8.5 million in professional services for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

nonop.heading: Non-interest expense
nonop.text:
The $8.2 million increase in non-interest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily resulted from increases of $7.5 million in salaries and employee benefits, $4.7 million in technology, communication and bank operations, $3.7 million in commercial lease depreciation and $1.7 million in other non-interest expense. These increases were offset in part by decreases of $4.5 million in professional fees and $3.8 million in FDIC assessments, non-income taxes and regulatory fees for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

The $25.7 million increase in non-interest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025 primarily resulted from increases of $26.4 million in salaries and employee benefits, $12.0 million in commercial lease depreciation, $7.5 million in technology, communication and bank operations and $4.7 million in other non-interest expense. These increases were offset in part by decreases of $14.6 million in FDIC assessments, non-income taxes and regulatory fees and $8.5 million in professional services for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

tax.heading: INCOME TAXES
tax.text:
The table below presents income tax expense and the effective tax rate for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025:

The $2.4 million decrease in income tax expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026, when compared to the same period in the prior year, primarily resulted from a lower effective tax rate, as pre-tax income was relatively consistent between periods. The decrease in the effective tax rate to 22.1% from 24.5% primarily resulted from favorable discrete items, primarily excess tax benefits on vested stock awards and the net discount realized on the purchase of energy tax credits, and a lower estimated annual effective tax rate.

The $19.2 million increase in income tax expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, when compared to the same period in the prior year, primarily resulted from higher pre-tax income. The effective tax rate was relatively consistent at 21.7% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, as the benefit of a lower estimated annual effective tax rate was offset by a smaller impact of favorable discrete items relative to pre-tax income. Favorable discrete items in 2026 primarily consisted of excess tax benefits on vested stock awards and the net discount realized on the purchase of energy tax credits.

net.text: Customers reported net income available to common shareholders of $78.4 million and $219.6 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income available to common shareholders of $73.7 million and $139.1 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. Factors contributing to the change in net income available to common shareholders for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 were as follows:

ocf.text: Cash provided by operating activities of $198.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 resulted from proceeds from sales and repayments of loans held for sale of $458.5 million, net income of $219.6 million and net non-cash operating adjustments of $96.9 million, partially offset by origination and purchases of loans held for sale of $436.0 million, an increase in accrued interest receivable and other assets of $91.0 million and a decrease in accrued interest payable and other liabilities of $49.1 million.

da.heading: Commercial lease depreciation
da.text:
The $3.7 million increase in commercial lease depreciation for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily resulted from the growth of the operating lease arrangements originated by Customers’ commercial equipment financing group in which Customers is the lessor.

The $12.0 million increase in commercial lease depreciation for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025 primarily resulted from the growth of the operating lease arrangements originated by Customers’ commercial equipment financing group in which Customers is the lessor.

sbc.text: The increases in common stock and additional paid in capital primarily resulted from the issuance of common stock under share-based compensation arrangements for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Net interest income.heading: Net interest income
Net interest income.text: Net interest income increased $6.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to higher average loan balances. Average interest-earning assets increased by $2.7 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in interest-earning assets was primarily driven by increases in corporate banking loans and leases and investment securities. NIM decreased by 27 basis points to 3.19% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from 3.46% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The NIM decrease was primarily attributable to lower market interest rates on corporate banking loans and leases and interest earning deposits and lower discount accretion on geographic and other commercial and industrial loans, partially offset by lower cost of deposits from a favorable shift in deposit mix and lower market interest rates for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

intro.text: Customers Bancorp is a bank holding company engaged in banking activities through its wholly owned subsidiary, Customers Bank, collectively referred to as “Customers” herein. Customers is a forward-thinking bank with strong risk management that provides commercial and consumer customers the stability and trust inherent in working with an established and regulated financial institution. The Bank has diversified lending activities that build overall franchise value and a high-tech, high-touch, branch-light strategy that serves its customers through a single-point-of-contact private banking strategy. The Bank serves commercial businesses, through community, SBA, and private client groups.
